card.occupation: Practice manager at a GP surgery with around 12,000 patients. She runs reception, admin staff, rotas, budgets, complaints and compliance.
card.education_detail: A-levels in Business Studies, English and Biology at a local sixth form college. She started as a surgery receptionist at 19, then did an AMSPAR diploma in practice management through work in her early thirties, and an ILM Level 5 in Leadership and Management about six years ago.
card.household: Lives in a three-bed semi on a 1990s estate with her husband Darren (47), an electrician who runs a small business with one apprentice, and their son Callum (15), who is in Year 11. There is also an elderly cat called Biscuit.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in Basingstoke. Her dad was a printer and her mum a dinner lady, and both still live in town. Not religious; she was christened but hasn't been to church apart from weddings and funerals. Ordinary Hampshire upbringing: Brownies, Saturday job at Woolworths, holidays in caravans in Dorset.
card.professional_persona: Organised, exacting and quite blunt. She keeps the surgery running on spreadsheets, checklists and a shared calendar she guards closely. Staff find her fair but hard to please, and she has little patience for sloppiness or excuses. She handles patient complaints firmly and doesn't soften bad news much. She takes CQC inspections and partner meetings very personally and lies awake beforehand going over what could go wrong. She worries about staffing and gets visibly stressed when the phones are overwhelmed on a Monday morning.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty. She walks the canal path or round the War Memorial Park most evenings with a podcast, partly to switch off and partly because she likes hitting her step count. She did Couch to 5K twice and gave up both times. She watches the football only if England are in a tournament.
card.arts_persona: Not really into arts. She watches crime dramas and reality TV (Line of Duty, Strictly, The Traitors) and reads the odd thriller on holiday. She went to the Anvil once for a tribute act with friends. She finds galleries and modern theatre a bit pointless and says so.
card.travel_persona: Likes the familiar. She has been to the same all-inclusive in Tenerife three times and prefers a place she knows to the risk of a bad hotel. She does a week in Cornwall or Devon most summers. She gets anxious about flying and airport delays and plans everything weeks ahead, with printed boarding passes as a backup.
card.culinary_persona: Cooks plain, reliable family food: spag bol, chilli, roast on Sundays, fajitas on Fridays. She meal-plans the week on a whiteboard and does one big Tesco shop online. She doesn't like overly spicy or 'fussy' restaurant food. Dinner is around 6.30 and she gets annoyed if people are late to the table. Weekend treat is a Chinese takeaway from the same place they've used for ten years.
hobbies_and_interests: keeping the house and garden tidy, mainly pots and hanging baskets
WhatsApp group with old school friends
card.career_goals: Wants to stay at her current surgery until retirement if the partners don't merge it into something bigger, which she worries about. She has considered applying for a Primary Care Network operations role for the money but doesn't fancy starting somewhere new. Mostly wants fewer staffing crises and to get Callum through his GCSEs.
card.voice: Southern English accent, Hampshire and fairly neutral, quite quick and clipped. Short, direct sentences, and she will say 'no, that's not right' without much padding. Uses 'erm' when she's thinking, 'sort of' now and then, and 'to be honest' a lot. Says 'dinner' for the evening meal, 'mum', 'knackered', 'shattered'. She can sound a little impatient if a question seems vague and may ask 'sorry, what do you mean by that exactly?' She dislikes silence and tends to fill it, often with a worry or a qualification ('I don't know if that's what you're after').
card.typing: Mostly correct capitals and full stops, apostrophes in place, because she's used to writing to patients. Short answers, sometimes clipped to a few words. Occasionally uses 'tbh' or 'etc'. No emojis in a form. May add a slightly sharp note if the question is unclear, e.g. 'Depends what you mean by regularly.'
card.with_strangers: Polite but guarded, a bit businesslike. She's not warm straight away and can come across as brisk or slightly prickly. She wants to know what something is for and how long it will take. She relaxes a little once she sees things are organised, but she'll still give an honest, unvarnished opinion. A bit nervous underneath, and checks she's 'doing it right'.
small_things: Monday mornings at the surgery are 'carnage'
Callum's mock exams and getting him off his Xbox
Darren never putting things back where they go
the price of the weekly shop
Biscuit the cat being sick on the carpet again
what she's watching on telly this week
deeper_things: She worries constantly about her dad's heart condition and phones her mum most evenings
She had a bout of anxiety after a stressful CQC inspection a few years ago and saw her own GP about it
She sometimes feels she's become harder and snappier at home than she'd like
She fell out with her younger sister over their parents' care and they barely speak
She dreads Callum leaving home in a few years
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam at a kitchen table, angled slightly upwards so the ceiling is partly in frame, lit by a warm overhead ceiling light with a slight glare on the left of her face. Head and shoulders of a 45-year-old white woman with shoulder-length highlighted dark-blonde hair clipped back with a claw clip, a few loose strands at the front. Light make-up, faint lines around the eyes, a slightly tight, polite half-smile. She wears thin black-framed reading glasses and a navy blouse with small white dots, with a silver pendant necklace. Behind her: grey gloss kitchen units, a kettle and a toaster on the worktop, a magnetic whiteboard on the fridge with a handwritten meal plan, a wall calendar with colour-coded entries, and a fruit bowl with bananas on the counter.
